facts.value: Bachelor of Architecture
Ancient Architecture - from Egyptian monumentality to Roman engineering.
Medieval Architecture - Romanesque solidity and Gothic verticality.
Islamic Architecture - geometry, courtyards, domes, ornament, and spatial sophistication.
Modern Architecture - efficiency, abstraction, and the logic of new materials.
Classical architecture grows out of Greek and Roman ideas of symmetry, columns, order, and measured proportion.
Gothic architecture is known for pointed arches, ribbed vaults, flying buttresses, stained glass, and a strong vertical pull.
Baroque architecture pushes drama, movement, contrast, ornament, and theatrical space.
Modern architecture strips away much of the ornament and focuses on efficiency, structure, light, material honesty, and function-driven form.
Postmodern architecture reacts against modernist restraint with color, irony, historical quotation, and deliberate complexity.
Islamic architecture is especially important for students studying geometry, ornament, courtyards, domes, light control, and the relationship between structure and pattern.
Sustainable architecture focuses on climate response, energy performance, material impact, water, and long-term building behavior.
Designing buildings and spatial systems.
Organizing layouts, circulation, structure, and envelope decisions.
Coordinating with clients, engineers, consultants, and builders.
Responding to code, safety, accessibility, and project constraints.
Balancing design ambition with budget, time, and constructability.
Creative thinking and problem-solving.
Technical competence in drawings, software, and construction logic.
Strong communication and collaboration.
Patience with revision, feedback, and coordination.
Clear visual organization and presentation skills.
